t: Born of Usman dan Fodio's Islamic reform jihad of 1804, the Sokoto Caliphate became the largest state in 19th-century West Africa.
Some thirty emirates shared one Islamic legal culture, a decentralised design that survived for almost a century without succession crises.
British forces with Maxim guns conquered it in 1903, then governed northern Nigeria through its emirs under indirect rule.
dyk: The last independent Sultan, Attahiru I, answered the British conquest with a hijra eastwards that deliberately echoed dan Fodio's founding migration.
ev: Usman dan Fodio makes his hijra to Gudu and declares jihad against the Hausa kings
Jihad forces storm Alkalawa, the Gobir capital, killing Sultan Yunfa
Dan Fodio dies; his son Muhammad Bello becomes Sultan of Sokoto
Britain charters the Royal Niger Company
Frederick Lugard proclaims the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria
British forces take Kano in February and occupy Sokoto in March
Sultan Attahiru I is killed fighting the British at Burmi in July
